BURSEVI:v9p274/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p274/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p274/r11.claim: The Qur’an is noble because it benefits worldly and afterlife life by containing essential knowledge, is honorable and excellent among books, and comes from the Noble through noble messengers to the noblest creation.
BURSEVI:v9p274/r11.anchor: إنه لقرءان كريم} هو المقسم عليه أي لكتاب كثير النفع

BURSEVI:v9p274/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p274/r12.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v9p274/r12.claim: Some say the Qur’an is noble because it directs people to noble morals, lofty concerns, and virtuous deeds.
BURSEVI:v9p274/r12.anchor: وقال بعضهم : كريم لأنه يدل على مكارم الأخلاق ومعالي الأمور

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p160/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p160/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p160/r4.claim: The oath bears witness that the Qur’an is exalted revelation from God, kept in a protected book and accessible only to pure, near angels, never to jinn or devils.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p160/r4.anchor: It is found in a protected book with the Almighty and no one except His pure angels can have access to it

QASHANI:56:73-82/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:56:73-82/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:56:73-82/r5.claim: The noble Qur’an is exalted, ancient, honorable comprehensive knowledge; its hidden book is the Prophet’s heart, where Qur’anic intellect is deposited beyond the senses except for purified angels.
QASHANI:56:73-82/r5.anchor: هو قلبه المكنون في الغيب عن الحواس وما عدا المقربين من الملائكة المطهرين

QUSHAYRI:v3p279/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p279/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p279/r5.claim: The Quran is noble because nobility excludes baseness; the author also says this means it is uncreated and that it guides noble character.
QUSHAYRI:v3p279/r5.anchor: والكرم نفي الدناءة - أي : أنه غير مخلوق

QUSHAYRI:v3p279/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p279/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p279/r6.claim: The Quran is noble because it comes from a generous Lord, through a noble Messenger and a noble angel.
QUSHAYRI:v3p279/r6.anchor: من عند رب كريم على رسول كريم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p92/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p92/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p92/r8.claim: Karīm is a laudatory description that excludes what does not befit the Qurʾān.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p92/r8.anchor: وكريم: وصف مدح ينفي عنه مالا يليق به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p92/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p92/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p92/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains karīm as excellent among scriptures, greatly beneficial, or honored by God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p92/r9.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: كريم: حسن مرضي في جنسه من الكتب، أو نفاع جم المنافع

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p22#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p22#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p22#2/r2.claim: The Qur’an is noble and honored because it is God’s speech; noble can mean giving abundant good.

BAYDAWI-FULL:56:76-79/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:56:76-79/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:56:76-79/r3.claim: The noble Qur’an is greatly beneficial because it contains essential principles for sound worldly and afterlife life, or is excellent and approved in its kind.
BAYDAWI-FULL:56:76-79/r3.anchor: كثير النفع لاشتماله على أصول العلوم المهمة في إصلاح المعاش والمعاد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p332/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p332/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p332/r5.claim: The pronoun in “it is a noble Quran” has no expressed antecedent because the Quran is already mentally present to the audience.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p332/r5.anchor: وضمير { إنه لقرآن كريم } راجع إلى غير مذكور في الكلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p332/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p332/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p332/r6.claim: Quran literally means recited speech, repeatedly read and contemplated; the author links this usage to another Quranic occurrence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p332/r6.anchor: والقرآن : الكلام المقروء ، أي المتلو المكرر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p332/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p332/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p332/r7.claim: Karim means precious and exalted; the Quran surpasses earlier divine books through comprehensive guidance, evidence, refutation, clarity, concision, eloquence, and sound.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p332/r7.anchor: والكريم : النفيس الرفيع في نوعه كما تقدم عند قوله تعالى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p251/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p251/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p251/r4.claim: The Quran is the object of the oath, and karīm affirms its praiseworthy qualities while denying defects.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p251/r4.anchor: وقوله: إنه لقرآن هو الذي وقع القسم عليه، ووصفه بالكرم على معنى إثبات صفات المدح له

JISHUMI:v9p6763#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6763#2/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6763#2/r6.claim: Speech is an accident that does not persist; it descends from its locus or from the locus of its sign.
JISHUMI:v9p6763#2/r6.anchor: والكلام: عرض لا يبقى، وإنما ينزل من محله أو محل أمارته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p466/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p466/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p466/r8.claim: The Qur'an is noble—excellent in its kind, beneficial, or honored by God—and the protected book is inaccessible to all but purified angels if it means the Preserved Tablet.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p466/r8.anchor: كريم حسن مرضي في جنسه من الكتب . أو نفاع جم المنافع . أو كريم على الله

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p462/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p462/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p462/r14.claim: The Qur'an is noble, beneficial, rich in noble character and lofty matters, and honors its memorizer and reciter.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p462/r14.anchor: كريم عند الله . الثاني : عظيم النفع للناس . الثالث : كريم بما فيه من كرائم الأخلاق

QURTUBI-FULL:56:75-77/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:75-77/r16.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:56:75-77/r16.claim: The pronoun in “it is surely a noble Quran” returns to the Quran itself.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:75-77/r16.anchor: قيل: إن الهاء تعود على القرآن أي إن القرآن لقسم عظيم، قاله ابن عباس وغيره.

TABATABAI:56:75-80/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:56:75-80/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:56:75-80/r6.claim: Because deniers reject both divine unity and resurrection through denying the Qur'an that teaches them, God first proves those truths, then affirms the Qur'an's divine origin.
TABATABAI:56:75-80/r6.anchor: فأورد تعالى أولا بيانا لإثبات أصل الوحدانية والبعث بذكر شواهد من آياته

TABATABAI:56:75-80/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:56:75-80/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:56:75-80/r7.claim: The Qur'an is noble and precious to God, praiseworthy in its qualities, and beneficial because its knowledge brings happiness in this life and the next.
TABATABAI:56:75-80/r7.anchor: ويستفاد من توصيفه بالكريم من غير تقييد في مقام المدح أنه كريم على الله عزيز عنده

TABRISI:56:75/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:56:75/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:56:75/r15.claim: The Quran is truly noble because its proofs yield abundant good and lead to truth; God's attribute of noble giver is eternal.
TABRISI:56:75/r15.anchor: فلما كان القرآن من شأنه أن يعطي الخير الكثير بأدلته المؤدية إلى الحق كان كريما على حقيقة معنى الكريم

THALABI:v9p218/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p218/r3.speaker: عبد العزيز بن يحيى الكناني
THALABI:v9p218/r3.claim: Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya al-Kinani says the Quran is uncreated.
THALABI:v9p218/r3.anchor: وقال عبد العزيز بن يحيى الكناني: غير مخلوق

THALABI:v9p218/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p218/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p218/r4.claim: Another explanation calls the Quran generous because its ease overcomes its difficulty.
THALABI:v9p218/r4.anchor: وقيل: سمي كريما لأن يسره يغلب عسره.

ELMALILI:56:75-96#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:56:75-96#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:56:75-96#2/r8.claim: Karīm can mean richly beneficial because the Qur’an contains key knowledge for life and the afterlife, beautiful and worthy of honor, or honored with God.
ELMALILI:56:75-96#2/r8.anchor: çok faydalı, feyizli, çünkü me‘âş ve me‘âda müte‘allik birçok mühim ilimlerin esaslarını muhtevîdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:75/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:75/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:75/r6.claim: Calling the Qur'an noble reflects its rank and value: as the final book it is perfected, protected from falsehood, rich in morals and important subjects, and a guide full of proof, knowledge, and wisdom.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:75/r6.anchor: Allah Teâlâ, son kitap olması dolayısıyla onu bütün ilâhî kitaplardan mükemmel kılmış, gerçek dışı unsurların ona karışmasını önlemiş

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p136/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p136/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p136/r2.claim: Verses 75–96 signal the Qur’an’s exalted status and its protection from Satan and his agents.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p136/r2.anchor: it is above and beyond the reach of Satan and his agents

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p136/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p136/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p136/r3.claim: Quraysh are cautioned not to ignore the sublime message and thereby bring doom upon themselves.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p136/r3.anchor: not to turn a deaf ear to this sublime message and invite their doom

BIQAI-FULL:v7p425/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p425/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p425/r1.claim: The Qur'an is comprehensive, accessible, explanatory of difficult matters, and rich in noble kinds of content.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p425/r1.anchor: أي جامع سهل قريب مفقه مبين للغوامض ذو أنواع جليلة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p425/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p425/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p425/r2.claim: Its nobility includes its transmission from the highest King to the best of creation through the Holy Spirit, in eloquent Arabic and in an inimitable form.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p425/r2.anchor: من كرمه كونه من الملك الأعلى إلى خير الخلق بسفارة روح القدس وبلسان العرب

JISHUMI:v9p6768/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6768/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6768/r6.claim: Calling the Quran a discourse, revelation, and guarded book, and saying it is not touched, shows it is originated rather than eternal, since these descriptions fit neither literal nor figurative eternity.
JISHUMI:v9p6768/r6.anchor: وتدل على حدث القرآن؛ لأنه وصفه بأنه حديث وتنزيل، وكتاب مكنون، ولا يمسه

TABRISI:56:83/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:56:83/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:56:83/r13.claim: The Qur’an is noble because it brings abundant benefits and great reward for reciting and acting on it.
TABRISI:56:83/r13.anchor: { إنه لقرآن كريم } معناه إن الذي تلوناه عليك لقرآن كريم أي عام المنافع كثير الخير

TABRISI:56:83/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:56:83/r14.speaker: مقاتل
TABRISI:56:83/r14.claim: Maqatil says the Qur’an is noble because God honored and exalted it.
TABRISI:56:83/r14.anchor: كريم عند الله تعالى أكرمه الله تعالى وأعزه لأنه كلامه عن مقاتل.

TABRISI:56:83/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:56:83/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:56:83/r15.claim: The Qur’an is noble because it is God’s speech, protected from alteration, inimitable, and filled with rulings, admonitions, and everything sublime or precious.
TABRISI:56:83/r15.anchor: ولأنه محفوظ عن التغيير والتبديل ولأنه معجز ولأنه يشتمل على الأحكام والمواعظ

RAZI-FULL:v29p165#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p165#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p165#2/r1.claim: The oath's object may be the Qur'an, which opponents called poetry or magic.
RAZI-FULL:v29p165#2/r1.anchor: القرآن كانوا يجعلونه تارة شعرا وأخرى سحرا وغير ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v29p165#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p165#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p165#2/r2.claim: The more apparent object is monotheism and resurrection.

RAZI-FULL:v29p165#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p165#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p165#3/r1.claim: The pronoun may refer to the already known revelation sent to Muhammad, which people called poetry or magic.
RAZI-FULL:v29p165#3/r1.anchor: إلى معلوم وهو الكلام الذي أنزل على محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v29p165#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p165#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p165#3/r2.claim: Alternatively, it refers to the preceding sura's discourse on monotheism, resurrection, their proofs, and the oath, which opponents called Muhammad's invention.
RAZI-FULL:v29p165#3/r2.anchor: إلى مذكور وهو جميع ما سبق في سورة الواقعة

RAZI-FULL:v29p165#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p165#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p165#3/r3.claim: Qurʾān may be a verbal noun used for its object, the recited text; Rāzī compares this usage to 13:31 and 31:11.
RAZI-FULL:v29p165#3/r3.anchor: مصدر أريد به المفعول وهو المقروء

RAZI-FULL:v29p165#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p165#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p165#3/r4.claim: Alternatively, Qurʾān is a noun for what is recited, like qurbān for what one offers devotionally and ḥulwān for what is given or tasted.
RAZI-FULL:v29p165#3/r4.anchor: اسم لما يقرأ كالقربان لما يتقرب به

RAZI-FULL:v29p165#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p165#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p165#3/r5.claim: This noun reading answers critics of jurists' zakat term al-jubrān: it can name the thing by which compensation is made, like Qurʾān names what is recited.
RAZI-FULL:v29p165#3/r5.anchor: هو اسم لما يجبر به كالقربان

RAZI-FULL:v29p165#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p165#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p165#3/r6.claim: One answer is that opponents rejected the whole description Qurʾān noble, not merely the fact that the text could be recited.
RAZI-FULL:v29p165#3/r6.anchor: فهم كانوا ينكرون كونه قرآنا كريما

RAZI-FULL:v29p165#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p165#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p165#3/r7.claim: Rāzī prefers that opponents called it invented: calling it a Qurʾān establishes that Muhammad received and recited it, and that it will be recited forever in this life and the next.
RAZI-FULL:v29p165#3/r7.anchor: أثبت كونه مقروءا على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ليقرأ ويتلى

RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r1.claim: Unlike ordinary speech that grows stale through repetition, the Qurʾān remains fresh forever; even angels who knew it long before Muhammad hear it with a new listener's delight.
RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r1.anchor: لا يهون بكثرة التلاوة ويبقى أبد الدهر كالكلام الغض والحديث الطري

RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r2.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r2.claim: A reported definition of karīm is something pure in origin and manifest in excellence; lineage or character alone does not capture the full sense.
RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r2.anchor: قيل : الكريم هو الذي كان طاهر الأصل ظاهر الفضل

RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r3.claim: Common usage narrows karam to easy or abundant giving because people prize what they receive; Rāzī calls this a bad custom and defines true nobility by purity of origin and evident excellence.
RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r3.anchor: الكريم هو الذي استجمع فيه ما ينبغي

RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r4.claim: The Qurʾān is noble in its pure source, manifest virtue, eloquent wording, and sound meaning.
RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r4.anchor: فالقرآن أيضا كريم بمعنى طاهر الأصل ظاهر الفضل لفظه فصيح

RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r5.claim: In ordinary usage too, the Qurʾān gives each seeker what they need: jurists, sages, and writers draw on it, and its wording is unusually easy to memorize and preserve exactly.

RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r6.claim: As ʿazīz, the Qurʾān leaves those who turn away with nothing, unlike other books whose meanings may remain after they are forgotten.
RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r6.anchor: ولكونه عزيزا أن كل من يعرض عنه لا يبقى معه منه شيء

RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r7.claim: As ḥakīm, it makes those who engage with it wholeheartedly independent of other sciences.
RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r7.anchor: ولكونه حكيما من اشتغل به وأقبل عليه بالقلب أغناه عن سائر العلوم

RAZI-FULL:v29p167/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p167/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p167/r9.claim: Calling it a Qurʾān rebuts the claim that Muhammad composed it himself.
RAZI-FULL:v29p167/r9.anchor: أن وصفه بكونه قرآنا صار ردا على من قال

STUDYQURAN:56:77/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:56:77/r1.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:56:77/r1.claim: The Noble Quran may refer to what has been discussed in this sūrah or to the Quran as a whole.
STUDYQURAN:56:77/r1.anchor: a reference to everything that has been mentioned thus far in this sūrah or to the whole of the Quran (R)

STUDYQURAN:56:77/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:56:77/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:56:77/r2.claim: Quran here may carry its linguistic sense of a noble recitation.
STUDYQURAN:56:77/r2.anchor: In this instance, Quran may be read according to its linguistic meaning

STUDYQURAN:56:77/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:56:77/r3.speaker: R, Sh
STUDYQURAN:56:77/r3.claim: Karīm indicates the combination of all praiseworthy attributes.
STUDYQURAN:56:77/r3.anchor: Noble translates karīm, which indicates the joining together of all praiseworthy attributes (R, Sh).

STUDYQURAN:56:77/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:56:77/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:56:77/r4.claim: What is noble is said to have pure origin and manifest bounty.
STUDYQURAN:56:77/r4.anchor: is said to be of pure origin

TABATABAI:2:21-25#14/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:21-25#14/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:21-25#14/r2.claim: Other verses depict the Qur'an as preserved in a guarded tablet, an exalted wise source, and a protected book; its meanings rest on enduring, unchanging realities.
TABATABAI:2:21-25#14/r2.anchor: فهذه الآيات ونظائرها تحكي عن إتكاء القرآن في معانيه على حقائق ثابتة غير متغيرة ولا متغير ما يتكي عليها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:56:77-78/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:56:77-78/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:56:77-78/r1.claim: The Qur’an is beautiful and noble, and mighty or precious.

BURHAN:v1p278/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p278/r1.speaker: الشافعى
BURHAN:v1p278/r1.claim: Al-Shafi'i, as reported by al-Wahidi, treats Quran as a proper, non-derived name for God's Book.
BURHAN:v1p278/r1.anchor: قال الواحدى قول الشافعى هو اسم لكتاب الله يعنى أنه اسم علم غير مشتق

BURHAN:v1p278/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p278/r2.speaker: الأشعرى
BURHAN:v1p278/r2.claim: Al-Ash'ari derives Quran from joining: it brings together its suras, verses, and letters, like qiran joins pilgrimage rites.
BURHAN:v1p278/r2.anchor: مشتق من قرنت الشىء بالشىء إذا ضممته إليه فسمى بذلك لقرآن السور والآيات والحروف فيه ومنه قيل للجمع بين الحج والعمرة قران قال وإلى هذا المعنى ذهب الأشعرى

BURHAN:v1p278/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p278/r3.speaker: القرطبى
BURHAN:v1p278/r3.claim: Al-Qurtubi derives the unhamzated form from qarā'in because Quranic verses confirm and resemble one another.
BURHAN:v1p278/r3.anchor: قال القرطبى القران بغير همز مأخوذ من القرائن لأن الآيات منه يصدق بعضها بعضا ويشابه بعضها بعضا

BURHAN:v1p278/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p278/r4.speaker: الزجاج
BURHAN:v1p278/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj rejects al-Qurtubi's derivation: the unhamzated pronunciation reflects ease, transferring the hamza vowel to the preceding consonant; al-Farisi noted this analysis.
BURHAN:v1p278/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج وهذا القول سهو والصحيح أن ترك الهمز فيه من باب التخفيف

BURHAN:v1p278/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p278/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p278/r8.claim: Kalam is linked to impact: speech is called kalam because it impresses on the listener's mind a benefit previously unknown to them.
BURHAN:v1p278/r8.anchor: وأما الكلام فمشتق من التأثير يقال كلمة إذا أثر فيه بالجرح فسمى الكلام كلاما لأنه يؤثر فى ذهن السامع فائدة لم تكن عنده

BURHAN:v1p278/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p278/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p278/r9.claim: The Quran is called light because it lets people discern subtle matters of the lawful and unlawful.
BURHAN:v1p278/r9.anchor: وأما النور فلأنه يدرك به غوامض الحلال والحرام

BURHAN:v1p278/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p278/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p278/r10.claim: It is called guidance because it clearly points to truth and distinguishes truth from falsehood.
BURHAN:v1p278/r10.anchor: وأما تسميته هدى فلأن فيه دلالة بينة إلى الحق وتفريقا بينه وبين الباطل

BURHAN:v1p278/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p278/r11.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p278/r11.claim: It is called remembrance for its exhortations, warnings, and accounts of past nations; dhikr is the verbal noun of remembering.
BURHAN:v1p278/r11.anchor: وأما تسميته ذكرا فلما فيه من المواعظ والتحذير وأخبار الأمم الماضية وهو مصدر ذكرت ذكرا

BURHAN:v1p278/r13.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p278/r13.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p278/r13.claim: It is called clarification because it explains the kinds of truth and lays out their proofs.
BURHAN:v1p278/r13.anchor: أما تسميته تبيانا فلأنه بين فيه أنواع الحق وكشف أدلته

BURHAN:v1p278/r14.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p278/r14.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p278/r14.claim: It is called a message because the Prophet's reports and delivery reached people through it.
BURHAN:v1p278/r14.anchor: أما تسميته بلاغا فلأنه لم يصل إليهم حال أخبار النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم وإبلاغه إليهم إلا به

BURHAN:v1p278/r15.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p278/r15.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p278/r15.claim: It is called manifest because it makes clear and separates truth from falsehood.
BURHAN:v1p278/r15.anchor: وأما تسميته مبينا فلأنه أبان وفرق بين الحق والباطل

BURHAN:v1p278/r16.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p278/r16.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p278/r16.claim: It is called bringer of glad tidings and warner because it promises Paradise and warns of the Fire.
BURHAN:v1p278/r16.anchor: وأما تسميته بشيرا ونذيرا فلأنه بشر بالجنة وأنذر من النار

BURHAN:v1p278/r17.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p278/r17.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p278/r17.claim: Aziz means that imitators cannot produce the Quran's like; the challenge concerns its reports and recitation in their striking composition, since eternal speech has no counterpart.
BURHAN:v1p278/r17.anchor: وأما تسميته عزيزا أى يعجز ويعز على من يروم أن يأتى بمثله فيتعذر ذلك عليه

BURHAN:v1p278/r18.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p278/r18.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p278/r18.claim: Another explanation of aziz is that a reciter who acts by the Quran is not humiliated.
BURHAN:v1p278/r18.anchor: وقيل المراد بالعزيز نفى المهانة عن قارئه إذا عمل به

BURHAN:v1p280/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p280/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p280/r1.claim: It is called Furqan because it distinguishes truth from falsehood and believers from unbelievers, including believers from hypocrites; this also explains Umar's title al-Faruq.
BURHAN:v1p280/r1.anchor: وأما تسميته فرقانا فلأنه فرق بين الحق والباطل والمسلم والكافر والمؤمن والمنافق وبه سمى عمر بن الخطاب الفارق

BURHAN:v1p280/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p280/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p280/r5.claim: Wahy means communicating something secretly, whether by speech to prophets or angels, inspiration to bees, or ants' signs; the term also connotes swift, hidden inspiration.
BURHAN:v1p280/r5.anchor: وأما تسميته وحيا ومعناه تعريف الشىء خفية سواء كان بالكلام كالأنبياء والملائكة أو بإلهام كالنحل وإشارة النمل

BURHAN:v1p280/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p280/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p280/r6.claim: It is called wise because its verses establish lawful and unlawful rulings and defy imitation; learning and practicing it restrains indecency.
BURHAN:v1p280/r6.anchor: وأما تسميته حكيما فلأن آياته أحكمت بذكر الحلال والحرام فأحكمت عن الإتيان بمثلها

BURHAN:v1p280/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p280/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p280/r7.claim: It is called confirming because it affirms earlier prophets or their scriptures before alteration.
BURHAN:v1p280/r7.anchor: وأما تسميته مصدقا فإنه صدق الأنبياء الماضين أو كتبهم قبل أن تغير وتبدل

BURHAN:v1p280/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p280/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p280/r8.claim: It is called a guardian because it testifies that earlier scriptures came from God.
BURHAN:v1p280/r8.anchor: وأما تسميته مهيمنا فلأنه الشاهد للكتب المتقدمة بأنها من عند الله

BURHAN:v1p280/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p280/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p280/r9.claim: The name balagh reflects its role in informing people, conveying the message, and delivering it.
BURHAN:v1p280/r9.anchor: وأما تسميته بلاغا فلأنه كان فى الإعلام والإبلاغ وأداء الرسالة

BURHAN:v1p280/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p280/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p280/r10.claim: It is called healing because faith cures unbelief and learning with practice cures ignorance.
BURHAN:v1p280/r10.anchor: وأما تسميته شفاء فلأنه من آمن به كان له شفاء من سقم الكفر ومن علمه وعمل به كان له شفاء من سقم الجهل

BURHAN:v1p280/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p280/r11.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p280/r11.claim: It is called mercy because understanding and comprehending it bring mercy to the person.
BURHAN:v1p280/r11.anchor: وأما تسميته رحمة فإن من فهمه وعقله كان رحمة له

BURHAN:v1p280/r12.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p280/r12.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p280/r12.claim: It is called stories because it recounts the reports and histories of earlier nations.
BURHAN:v1p280/r12.anchor: وأما تسميته قصصا فلأن فيه قصص الأمم الماضين وأخبارهم

BURHAN:v1p280/r13.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p280/r13.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p280/r13.claim: Majid means noble; part of the Quran's nobility is its preservation from alteration, addition, and subtraction.
BURHAN:v1p280/r13.anchor: وأم تسميته مجيدا والمجيد الشريف فمن شرفه أنه حفظ عن التغيير والتبديل والزيادة والنقصان

BURHAN:v1p280/r14.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p280/r14.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p280/r14.claim: The Quran is itself miraculous in that no one can produce its like.
BURHAN:v1p280/r14.anchor: وجعله معجزا فى نفسه عن أن يؤتى بمثله

BURHAN:v1p280/r15.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p280/r15.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p280/r15.claim: Tanzil is the verbal noun of revelation: God made Gabriel hear and understand His speech as He willed, without description or modality, and Gabriel conveyed it to the Prophet as learned.
BURHAN:v1p280/r15.anchor: وأما تسميته تنزيلا فلأنه مصدر نزلته لأنه منزل من عند الله على لسان جبريل لأن الله تعالى أسمع جبريل كلامه وفهمه إياه كما شاء من غير وصف ولا كيفية

BURHAN:v1p280/r17.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p280/r17.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p280/r17.claim: Dhikra reminds believers of the oneness of God on which He created them.
BURHAN:v1p280/r17.anchor: وأما تسميته ذكرى فلأنه ذكر للمؤمنين ما فطرهم الله عليه من التوحيد

BURHAN:v1p273/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p273/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p273/r1.claim: Zarkashī catalogs Qur’anic names including admonition, reminder, noble, exalted, wisdom, wise, guardian, blessed, and the rope of God.

BURHAN:v1p271/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p271/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p271/r1.claim: The opening letters fit each sura's vocabulary: compared with similarly sized suras, words built from that sura's opening letters recur more often, making another opening unsuitable.
BURHAN:v1p271/r1.anchor: وجدت الحروف المفتتح بها تلك السورة إفرادا وتركيبا أكثر عددا فى كلماتها منها فى نظيرتها ومماثلتها فى عدد كلمها وحروفها

BURHAN:v1p271/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p271/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p271/r2.claim: Al-Harali catalogued more than ninety Qur'an names; Qadi Abu al-Ma'ali counted fifty-five, including Book, Qur'an, Speech, Light, Guidance, Mercy, Criterion, and Healing.
BURHAN:v1p271/r2.anchor: وقال القاضى أبو المعالى عزيزى بن عبد الملك رحمه الله اعلم أن الله تعالى سمى القرآن بخمسة وخمسين اسما

BURHAN:v3p63/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p63/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p63/r6.claim: The author rejects that restriction: parenthetical clauses can occur with or without wāw, and the passage combines both forms.
BURHAN:v3p63/r6.anchor: وليس كما قال فقد يأتي بالواو كما سبق في الأمثلة وبدونها كقوله سبحانه

BURHAN:v1p276/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p276/r4.speaker: بعضهم
BURHAN:v1p276/r4.claim: Some hold that Qur'an is an un-derived proper name for God's speech.
BURHAN:v1p276/r4.anchor: فقيل هو اسم غير مشتق من شىء بل هو اسم خاص بكلام الله

BURHAN:v1p276/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p276/r5.speaker: الجوهرى
BURHAN:v1p276/r5.claim: Al-Jawhari and others derive Qur'an from qar', meaning to gather.
BURHAN:v1p276/r5.anchor: وقيل مشتق من القرى وهو الجمع ومنه قريت الماء فى الحوض أى جمعته قاله الجوهرى وغيره

BURHAN:v1p276/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p276/r6.speaker: الراغب
BURHAN:v1p276/r6.claim: Al-Raghib cautions that not every collection, or collection of any speech, is called Qur'an; the author suggests this may concern customary usage rather than the word's origin.
BURHAN:v1p276/r6.anchor: وقال الراغب لا يقال لكل جمع قرآن ولا لجمع كل كلام قرآن ولعل مراده بذلك فى العرف والاستعمال لا أصل اللغة

BURHAN:v1p276/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p276/r7.speaker: الهروى
BURHAN:v1p276/r7.claim: Al-Harawi says anything one gathers has been read.
BURHAN:v1p276/r7.anchor: وقال الهروى كل شىء جمعته فقد قرأته

BURHAN:v1p276/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p276/r8.speaker: أبو عبيد
BURHAN:v1p276/r8.claim: Abu Ubayd says the Qur'an is named for gathering its suras together.
BURHAN:v1p276/r8.anchor: وقال أبو عبيد سمى القرآن قرآنا لأنه جمع السور بعضها إلى بعض

BURHAN:v1p276/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p276/r9.speaker: الراغب
BURHAN:v1p276/r9.claim: Al-Raghib says the Qur'an gathers the fruits of earlier revealed books.
BURHAN:v1p276/r9.anchor: وقال الراغب سمى قرآنا لكونه جمع ثمرات الكتب المنزلة السابقة

BURHAN:v1p276/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p276/r10.speaker: بعض المتأخرين
BURHAN:v1p276/r10.claim: A later scholar rejects the root sense “gather”: 75:17 distinguishes gathering from Qur'an, which he derives from making manifest and articulating.
BURHAN:v1p276/r10.anchor: وقال بعض المتأخرين لا يكون القرآن و قرأ مادته بمعنى جمع

BURHAN:v1p276/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p276/r11.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p276/r11.claim: Another proposed derivation names the Qur'an for being read and recited, with its parts read in sequence.
BURHAN:v1p276/r11.anchor: وقيل سمى قرآنا لأن القراءة عنه والتلاوة منه وقد قرئت بعضها عن بعض

BURHAN:v1p276/r12.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p276/r12.speaker: إسماعيل بن قسطنطين
BURHAN:v1p276/r12.claim: In al-Shafi'i's biography, Isma'il ibn Qustantine says القرآن is an unhamzated proper name, not a derivative of قرأت; otherwise every recited text would be Qur'an.
BURHAN:v1p276/r12.anchor: وكان يقول القران اسم وليس مهموزا ولم يؤخذ من قرأت ولو أخذ من قرأت لكان كل ما قرىء قرآنا

BURHAN:v1p276/r13.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p276/r13.speaker: البيهقى
BURHAN:v1p276/r13.claim: Al-Bayhaqi says al-Shafi'i pronounced قرأت with hamza but Qur'an without it; al-Wahidi also says Ibn Kathir read it without hamza.
BURHAN:v1p276/r13.anchor: قال البيهقى كان الشافعى يهمز قرأت ولا يهمز القران ويقول هو اسم لكتاب الله غير مهموز

SULAMI:v2p302#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p302#2/r1.speaker: author
SULAMI:v2p302#2/r1.claim: One explanation is that the noble Quran points toward noble character, lofty matters, and honorable deeds.
SULAMI:v2p302#2/r1.anchor: قال : يدل على مكارم الأخلاق ومعالي الأمور وشريف الأفعال

SULAMI:v2p302#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p302#2/r2.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v2p302#2/r2.claim: Another explanation calls it noble because it descended from the Noble through a noble intermediary to the noblest of all creatures.
SULAMI:v2p302#2/r2.anchor: وقيل : قرآن كريم بنزوله من كريم بواسطة كريم إلى اكرم الخلق أجمعين

ITQAN:v1p143/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p143/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p143/r1.claim: He lists many Qur’anic titles: the firmest handhold, truth, justice, command, herald, glad tidings, glorious, Psalms, bearer of good news and warning, mighty, proclamation, and stories.
ITQAN:v1p143/r1.anchor: ومجيدا ﴿ بل هو قرآن مجيد ﴾ وزبورا ﴿ ولقد كتبنا في الزبور ﴾ وبشيرا ونذيرا

ITQAN:v1p143/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p143/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p143/r3.claim: Al-mubīn is so named because it makes the truth distinct from falsehood.
ITQAN:v1p143/r3.anchor: والمبين لأنه أبان أي أظهر الحق من الباطل

ITQAN:v1p143/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p143/r4.speaker: جماعة
ITQAN:v1p143/r4.claim: A group treats Qur’an as a proper name specific to God’s speech, not derived from another word, and therefore unhamzated.
ITQAN:v1p143/r4.anchor: هو اسم علم غير مشتق خاص بكلام الله فهو غير مهموز

ITQAN:v1p143/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p143/r5.speaker: الشافعي
ITQAN:v1p143/r5.claim: Al-Shafi‘i reportedly hamzated قرأت but not القرآن, treating Qur’an as a proper name like Torah and Gospel; Ibn Kathir also read it without hamza.
ITQAN:v1p143/r5.anchor: عن الشافعي أخرج البيهقي والخطيب وغيرهما عنه أنه كان يهمز قرأت ولا يهمز القرآن

ITQAN:v1p143/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p143/r6.speaker: الأشعري
ITQAN:v1p143/r6.claim: Al-Ash‘ari derives Qur’an from قرنت, joining things, because the text joins its suras, verses, and letters.
ITQAN:v1p143/r6.anchor: هو مشتق من قرنت الشيء بالشيء إذا ضممت أحدهما إلى الآخر وسمي به لقران السور والآيات والحروف فيه

ITQAN:v1p143/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p143/r7.speaker: الفراء
ITQAN:v1p143/r7.claim: Al-Farra’ derives Qur’an from القرائن: its verses corroborate and resemble one another; on this account its nūn is radical and it is unhamzated.
ITQAN:v1p143/r7.anchor: هو مشتق من القرائن لأن الآيات منه يصدق بعضها بعضا ويشابه بعضها بعضا وهي قرائن

ITQAN:v1p143/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p143/r8.speaker: الزجاج
ITQAN:v1p143/r8.claim: Al-Zajjaj rejects the قرائن derivation as mistaken; he explains the unhamzated form as hamza-lightening with its vowel transferred to the preceding consonant.
ITQAN:v1p143/r8.anchor: قال الزجاج هذا القول سهو والصحيح أن ترك الهمزة فيه من باب التخفيف ونقل حركة الهمزة

ITQAN:v1p143/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p143/r9.speaker: اللحياني
ITQAN:v1p143/r9.claim: Al-Lihyani calls Qur’an a verbal noun of قرأت, used for the read book by naming the object with its verbal noun.
ITQAN:v1p143/r9.anchor: هو مصدر لقرأت كالرجحان والغفران سمي به الكتاب المقروء من باب تسمية المفعول بالمصدر

ITQAN:v1p143/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p143/r10.speaker: الزجاج
ITQAN:v1p143/r10.claim: Another derivation, also attributed to al-Zajjaj, makes Qur’an a fa‘lān descriptor from qar’ meaning collection, as in gathering water in a basin.
ITQAN:v1p143/r10.anchor: هو وصف على فعلان مشتق من القرء بمعنى الجمع ومنه قرات الماء في الحوض أي جمعته

ITQAN:v3p201/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p201/r1.speaker: قدامة
ITQAN:v3p201/r1.claim: Qudama calls الاعتراض الالتفات: one or more syntactically ungoverned clauses inserted within connected speech for a purpose other than removing ambiguity.
ITQAN:v3p201/r1.anchor: وسماه قدامة التفاتا وهو الإتيان بجملة أو أكثر لا محل لها من الإعراب في أثناء كلام

ITQAN:v3p201/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p201/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p201/r8.claim: In the oath passage, وإنه لقسم and لو تعلمون interrupt the oath and its description, magnifying the sworn subject and stressing a grandeur beyond their knowledge.
ITQAN:v3p201/r8.anchor: تعظيما للمقسم به وتحقيقا لإجلاله وإعلاما لهم بأن له عظمة لا يعلمونها

ITQAN:v3p201/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p201/r9.speaker: الطيبي
ITQAN:v3p201/r9.claim: Al-Tibi says an interruption is effective because it conveys useful meaning while arriving unexpectedly, like a benefit received from where one did not expect it.
ITQAN:v3p201/r9.anchor: ووجه حسن الاعتراض حسن الإفادة مع أن مجيئه مجيء ما لا يترقب فكون كالحسنة تأتيك

QIRAAT-ER:56:77:3#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:56:77:3#1/r1.speaker: Ibn Kathīr and others
QIRAAT-ER:56:77:3#1/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr and other readers drop or soften the hamza in qurʾān to qurān; the source describes this as standard Ḥijāzī practice.
QIRAAT-ER:56:77:3#1/r1.anchor: attested in the reading of Ibn Kathīr and others. This softening of the hamza was standard Ḥijāzī practice

ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r1.claim: Calling it a noble Qur’an glorifies and confirms the preceding oath.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r1.anchor: وهو تعظيم للقسم مقرر مؤكد له

ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r2.claim: The parenthetical لو تعلمون falls between the adjective and the noun and intensifies the glorification; its unanswered conditional either denies their knowledge or implies that they would revere it or act accordingly.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r2.anchor: وقوله عز وجل ( لو تعلمون ) معترض بين الصفة والموصوف وهو تأكيد لذلك التعظيم وجواب ( لو ) إما متروك

ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r3.claim: The greatness of the oath has been indicated earlier, and is especially clear if مواقع النجوم is understood as Ibn Abbas and others transmitted.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r3.anchor: ووجه كون ذلك القسم عظيما قد أشير إليه فيما مر أو هو ظاهر بناءا على أن المراد ( بمواقع النجوم ) ما روي عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r4.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r4.claim: Al-Tibi explains كريم as excellent and pleasing among its kind of books, or as abundantly beneficial; the benefit fits a Qur’an containing foundational knowledge for this life and the next, with generosity used metaphorically.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r4.anchor: ومعنى كون القرآن كريما أنه حسن مرضي في جنسه كمن الكتب أو نفاع جم المنافع

ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r5.claim: Another view takes generosity broadly to include praiseworthy qualities such as great benefit, making the description literal.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : الكرم أعم من كثرة البذل والإحسان والاتصاف بما يحمد من الأوصاف

ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r6.claim: It may also mean noble in God’s sight; the author says this returns to the prior sense and requires an unnecessary implied preposition.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r6.anchor: وجوز أن يراد كريم على الله تعالى قيل : وهو يرجع لما تقدم

ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r7.claim: The pronoun refers to the Qur’an itself, not merely to its status as a recitation; the point is that it was revealed to the Prophet rather than composed by him, as disbelievers claimed.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r7.anchor: قيل : إن مرجع الضمير هو القرآن لا من حيث عنوان كونه قرآنا فبمجرد الأخبار عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r1.speaker: إبن خلكان
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r1.claim: Ibn Khallikan records that after Saladin captured Aleppo, judge Muhyi al-Din recited a poem predicting Jerusalem's conquest in Rajab, following the Aleppo victory in Safar.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r1.anchor: ذكر إبن خلكان في تاريخه أن السلطان صلاح الدين لما فتح مدينة حلب أنشد القاضي محيي الدين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r2.speaker: القاضي محيي الدين
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r2.claim: Asked how he made the prediction, Muhyi al-Din said he derived it from Ibn Barjan's tafsir of 30:2–4; the historian later found that commentary and its calculation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r2.anchor: فسئل القاضي من أين لك هذا فقال أخذته من تفسير إبن برجان

ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r3.speaker: إبن الكمال
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r3.claim: A well-known example is Ibn al-Kamal's inference that Sultan Selim would conquer Egypt from 21:105.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r3.anchor: ومن المشهور إستنباط إبن الكمال فتح مصر على يد السلطان سليم من قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r4.claim: Al-Alusi urges fairness toward Sufi masters in the Muhammadan spiritual circle and suspicion of one's own limited understanding when obstacles prevent access to their insights; he compares this to trusting those who saw the crescent.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r4.anchor: فالأنصاف كل الإنصاف التسليم للسادة الصوفية الذين هم مركز للدائرة المحمدية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r5.speaker: شيدلة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r5.claim: Shidla counts fifty-five names for the Quran, and al-Suyuti discusses the reasons for these names in al-Itqan.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r5.anchor: أن لكتاب الله تعالى أسماء أنهاها شيدلة في البرهان إلى خمسة وخمسين أسما

ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r6.claim: Al-Alusi says the many Quranic names ultimately reduce to Quran and Furqan, just as the divine names return to the attributes of beauty and majesty.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r6.anchor: وعندي أنها كلها ترجع بعد التأمل الصادق إلى القرآن والفرقان رجوع أسماء الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r7.speaker: الشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r7.claim: Al-Shafi'i and a group hold that Quran is a proper, non-derived name specific to the revelation to Muhammad, unhamzated and treated as a definite name.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r7.anchor: المروي عن الشافعي وبه قال جماعة أنه اسم علم غير مشتق خاص بهذا الكلام المنزل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r8.speaker: الأشعري
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r8.claim: Al-Ashari and others derive Quran from qarantu, 'I joined,' because its suras, verses, and letters are joined together; on this view it has no hamza and its n is original.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r8.anchor: والمنقول عن الأشعري وأقوام أنه مشتق من قرنت الشيء إذا ضممته إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r9.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r9.claim: Al-Farra derives Quran from qara'in, 'indications,' because its verses confirm and resemble one another; this derivation also has no hamza and treats n as original.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r9.anchor: وقال الفراء هو مشتق من القرائن لأن الآيات فيه يصدق بعضها بعضا ويشبه بعضها بعضا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r10.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r10.claim: Al-Zajjaj rejects the unhamzated derivations and treats the hamza as original, explaining its omission as lightening with the vowel transferred to the preceding letter; he derives the word from qarʾ, gathering.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r10.anchor: وقال الزجاج هذا القول غلط والصواب أن ترك الهمزة فيه من باب التخفيف ونقل حركتها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r11.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r11.claim: Abu Ubayda explains the name as referring to the gathering of the suras.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r11.anchor: وسمى به لأنه جمع السور كما قال أبو عبيدة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r12.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r12.claim: Al-Raghib explains Quran as a gathering of the fruits of earlier scriptures.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r12.anchor: أو ثمرات الكتب السالفة كما قال الراغب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r13.speaker: قطرب
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r13.claim: Qutrub connects Quran to the reciter bringing it out from his mouth, using the expression that a she-camel has never brought forth a fetal membrane.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r13.anchor: لأن القاريء يظهره من فيه أخذا من قولهم ما قرأت الناقة سلى قط كما حكى عن قطرب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r14.speaker: اللحياني
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r14.claim: Al-Lihyani and others regard Quran as a verbal noun like ghufran, used for the thing recited by naming the object with its verbal noun.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r14.anchor: وعند اللحياني وجماعة هو مصدر كالغفران سمى به المقروء تسمية المفعول بالمصدر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r15.speaker: السيوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r15.claim: Al-Suyuti chooses al-Shafi'i's account, which al-Alusi criticizes as unargued deference to the imam of his legal school.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r15.anchor: قال السيوطي : قلت والمختار عندي في هذه المسألة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r16.claim: Al-Alusi finds al-Zajjaj's analysis more convincing because hamza is the common form and six of the seven readers pronounce it; al-Zajjaj explains dropping the hamza but not retaining it, and al-Alusi begins to call Quran originally an adjective or verbal noun.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7#3/r16.anchor: قول الزجاج أرق من وجه إذ الشائع فيه الهمز وبه قرأ السبعة ما عدا إبن كثير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p151#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p151#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p151#2/r1.claim: Karīm is a comprehensive name for praiseworthy qualities: the Qur’an contains explanation, guidance, and wisdom and is honored by God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p151#2/r1.anchor: والكريم اسم جامع لما يحمد وذلك أن فيه البيان والهدى والحكمة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p543#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p543#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p543#2/r3.claim: Some exegetes treat la as extra, yielding “I swear by the positions of the stars,” with “it is a noble Quran” as the oath’s response; al-Tabari transmits this from Saʿid ibn Jubayr.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p543#2/r3.anchor: ورواه ابن جرير، عن سعيد بن جبير. ويكون جوابه: {إنه لقرآن كريم}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p543#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p543#2/r4.speaker: مفسرون آخرون
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p543#2/r4.claim: Other exegetes say la is meaningful at the start of an oath responding to a denial: the Quran is not sorcery or soothsaying, but a noble Quran; Aisha uses the same oath form.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p543#2/r4.anchor: وقال آخرون: ليست "لا" زائدة لا معنى لها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p543#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p543#2/r5.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p543#2/r5.claim: Al-Tabari cites Arabists who read the opening as “the matter is not as you claim,” then a fresh oath begins.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p543#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن جرير: وقال بعض أهل العربية: معنى قوله: {فلا أقسم} فليس الأمر كما تقولون، ثم استأنف القسم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p544/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p544/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p544/r1.claim: The oath is tremendous; if people knew its greatness, they would magnify what is sworn for, namely that the Quran revealed to Muhammad is a great and noble book.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p544/r1.anchor: {وإنه لقسم لو تعلمون عظيم} أي: وإن هذا القسم الذي أقسمت به لقسم عظيم

MUJAHID:v2p652#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p652#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p652#2/r1.claim: Mujahid explains the noble Qur'an as the Qur'an from God's Book.
MUJAHID:v2p652#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ لقرآن كريم ﴾ قال يقول القرآن من كتابي

NASAFI-FULL:v4p212#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p212#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p212#2/r1.claim: Karīm can mean good and pleasing, very beneficial and abundant in benefits, or honored by Allah.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p212#2/r1.anchor: حسن مرضى أو نفاع جم المنافع أوكريم على الله

NASAFI-FULL:v4p212#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p212#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p212#2/r2.claim: The phrase “if you only knew” interrupts between the described noun and its adjective.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p212#2/r2.anchor: واعترض بلو تعلمون بين الموصوف وصفته

QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r1.claim: The verse states the oath's answer: this is a noble Qur'an, neither magic, soothsaying, nor fabrication, but a praiseworthy revelation and a miracle given to the Prophet.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r1.anchor: أي أقسم بمواقع النجوم إن هذا القرآن قرآن كريم، ليس بسحر ولا كهانة، وليس بمفترى

QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r2.claim: The Qur'an is honored by believers as their Lord's speech and as a healing for their hearts, and by the people of heaven as their Lord's revelation.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r2.anchor: وهو كريم على المؤمنين، لأنه كلام ربهم، وشفاء صدورهم كريم على أهل السماء

QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r3.claim: One interpretation of karīm is that the Qur'an is uncreated.

QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r4.claim: Another interpretation calls it noble for its noble character and weighty meanings.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r4.anchor: وقيل: { كريم } لما فيه من كريم الأخلاق ومعاني الأمور.

QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r5.claim: Another explanation says the Qur'an honors its memorizer and magnifies its reciter.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r5.anchor: وقيل: لأنه يكرم حافظه، ويعظم قارئه.
